text:
The doctor is not skilled and cannot analyze clearly. My original filling fell out and I had to have it filled here. It turned out that I couldn't use it and my teeth were always sensitive when I chewed. I went in for 2-3 rounds of corrections, and they didn't work. I had to endure it for a year. In the end, it still didn't work, so I went back for a new look. The doctor told me to endure it or to dismantle and redo it, but there would be a cost. Who would endure it? They could dismantle and redo it, but the reason I endured it for a year is because the clinic didn't want to take any responsibility. They just said it had already been a year. However, the second time they dismantled and redoed it, the teeth were better because the doctor primed the teeth. But then again, why didn't they do a good job from the first time? The price quoted was 200 baht per tooth for the primer, but when they actually did it, they quoted 200 baht for the primer material on both sides, which is never the same as the quoted price. Furthermore, I had to pay more than usual. And from what I've observed, whenever something is done, there are always additional costs. They collect on small things, causing the price to increase from the quoted price. Most recently, I went for an airflow procedure and they quoted one price, but when it was finished, they charged another price because there were add-ons. Most importantly, the add-on prices were not informed before or during the procedure. It's like forcing my hands. They always add more after the procedure. At other places, they'll inform you and ask you exactly what you're going to do, whether you want it done or not. Here, they'll do it properly and then inform you. They seem to charge a reasonable price, but when it's actually done, they always add on and add on. They're just trying to be smooth.

P.S. This answer isn't a smooth lie. After my first filling, they told me I didn't keep my appointment. A week after my first filling, I went back to a female dentist to fix the sensitivity. It didn't fix it, and it was still as sensitive as ever. If the clinic is truly responsible, why didn't they fix it right then? Why did they force me to use it? After another 1-2 months, I was annoyed, so I went back again. This time, I saw a male dentist. He only managed to grind it down a little because my teeth weren't high anymore, but the sensitivity was still there. It was the same sensitivity from the poor filling, but they didn't have anything to fix it. Look at my history. After that, I've been chewing constantly, and I endured it for a year. I only went to get it fixed last week. They told me I didn't show up for my follow-up appointment. Is that wrong? I went to the dentist the first week after the filling, and it didn't work. I had no reason not to go. Otherwise, last week, I would have gone to the dentist to fix it and pay again for it. This shows their insincerity. They're just after the benefits. A tube of composite filling is only a few hundred baht, and they still haven't fixed it. Anyone considering this service should think carefully. The quoted price for a dental implant is 200 baht per tooth, but the actual cost is 400 baht, as shown in the picture. They're just taking advantage and not willing to pay anything, even though they're doing a terrible job.

Regarding the additional charge for the airflow procedure, which you said the doctor informed you about, do you know what the doctor said? "Open your mouth first, I'll clean your teeth." That's all they said. If that's your explanation, let others consider whether it's a vague explanation. I thought it was a normal airflow procedure, not a supplementary procedure, and it would cost an additional 300 baht. Oh well, honesty doesn't last forever, dishonesty won't last long.

Just because you assume the doctor approves of this and that doesn't mean I agree with everything. The doctor isn't doing it for free. I'm going to get the airflow because I'm happy with it, and there's no need to push anything else.
